chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ja'fi, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and a letter came to him from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik regarding a man who dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and married her. The people had differed regarding us here: one group said, 'Kill him,' and another group said, 'Burn him.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'The sanctity of the dead is like the sanctity of the living. His punishment is that his hand be cut off for digging her up and stripping her of her clothes, and the punishment for fornication is established against him; if he were married, he would be stoned, and if he were not married, he would be flogged one hundred times.'

key_terms.إِحْصَان: being married (in the context of legal punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for digging up a dead woman and marrying her according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the sanctity of the deceased is equated to that of the living, establishing that digging up a corpse and stripping her clothes incurs the hadd punishment of hand amputation. Furthermore, the subsequent marriage is treated as fornication, subjecting the perpetrator to stoning if he was previously married (muhsan) or flogging if not, thereby clarifying the legal distinction between the theft of the body and the sexual act.
